title: 🪙 'Hashi' Launches 'HBTC' — Your Bitcoin Stays Put and Works for You!
body: 🪙 'Hashi' Launches 'HBTC' — Your Bitcoin Stays Put and Works for You!

The "Sui" network announced on November 19 the launch of "Hashi", a new financial layer for Bitcoin running on the mainnet, with more than 20 partners in custody, lending, and decentralized finance. The idea is simple and different: your Bitcoin stays on the Bitcoin network itself, while "HBTC" coins are minted on "Sui" at a one-to-one ratio for every deposited Bitcoin, so you can use them as collateral or in lending and vaults without selling your coins.

Uses began immediately: the "Fluid" platform lets you pledge "HBTC" and borrow a stablecoin against it, while "Upshift" manages investment vaults and "Honey B" offers strategies linked to real-world assets and public markets. On the institutional side, "Anchorage Digital" will support custody of "HBTC" and stablecoins and their deployment, with "BitGo" to follow later, plus liquidity from "Cumberland" and "Wave Digital Assets". The network had announced in October capital commitments from partners exceeding $500 million.

Notably, the system has no token of its own: there is no "Hashi" coin, no presale, and no airdrop — any offer of that kind is fake. Deposits also require six confirmations on the Bitcoin network before "HBTC" is minted, and governance is managed through the voting weight of "Sui" validators themselves.
Simply put: Bitcoin used to sit in the wallet doing nothing; now you can borrow stable dollars against it or put it in investment vaults, without selling a single coin.
Would you rather your Bitcoin stay a store of value only, or work for you as collateral?
